Done in src/storage/mod.rs only (commit a376bbe), net +6 lines. Db no longer carries a second implementation of transaction semantics: it now supplies just the four TxnHost accessors (txn/wal/flush/discard) and wires the frozen §3 methods through — Storage::begin -> TxnHost::begin, commit -> TxnHost::commit, rollback -> TxnHost::rollback, all three mutators AND both DDL statements inside statement(), Db::open through recover(). Deleted stmt_txn, finish_stmt, commit_txn, the inherent recover(), and the Option<u64> + next_txn pair; the wal.commit-then-flush ordering now exists once, in txn.rs, with no copy in storage/mod.rs. discard() is my existing discard-by-reopen (drops the dirty map, the allocate_page-inflated page_count, and the heap/btree state above the pager). DEDUP, NOT A BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, as the orchestrator required: 353/353 corpus (122 statement ok / 49 statement error / 182 query, 441 rows compared) before and after, 224 lib tests, cargo test --test recovery 3/3, clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, cargo fmt clean, all from the repo root with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$HOME/.cache/quern-target/storage-trait and TMPDIR=$HOME/.tmpx. Two things worth knowing. (1) My TxnHost::flush() is pager.flush() AND wal.checkpoint(), not just Pager::flush: TxnHost::commit leaves the committed records in the log, Db::open calls recover() which re-applies them on top of pages that already hold them, and re-applying an insert allocates a fresh RowId (txn.rs documents that replay is not idempotent), so a clean commit + reopen would double every row — commit_persists_across_a_reopen catches it. flush() is the moment the checkpoint's precondition becomes true and txn.rs calls it from both commit and recover, so one impl covers both paths without duplicating a sequence. The constraint that creates: flush() must not be called while a txn is open. Today it is only reached from commit (txn just ended) and recover (no txn), so the invariant holds; messaged txn-impl on thread pact-msg-da91aace405caaca in case txn.rs ever grows a mid-transaction flush, offering to move the seam back to my call sites. (2) DDL is deliberately NOT inside plan/mod.rs's atomic() (§6), so it uses Db's own implicit txn via statement(); the txn_ddl replay in Storage::rollback that fixed bd_30-agents-a1z still works because statement()'s failure path calls TxnHost::rollback, not Storage::rollback, so DDL is never replayed on a failed statement. Nothing in src/txn.rs was changed or needed changing. No pact or bd command was perceptibly slow.

THE EXCLUSION THAT LIFTED, and what it bought. §6c caps nesting in the SHARED front end, so a deep program is now a Parse error both engines inherit instead of a SIGABRT that leaves no Output. Added Flavor::Deep, which opens a program with one deep shape drawn from two tables that straddle the two limits — they are different quantities and neither bounds the other, which is why there are two:
  CHAIN_LENS 1..12000 straddles MAX_EXPR_DEPTH=10000 (left-nested chain: nesting 1, tree depth N)
  NEST_LENS  1..400   straddles MAX_NEST=100         (parens/nested calls: nesting N, tree depth 1 or N)
Shapes: Int chain, Str chain (concatenation, so buffer growth is stressed as well as depth), paren stack, and nested identity calls — the last so a 99-level success and a 101-level refusal are told apart by their OUTPUT and not only by their error. Measured on the wide run: 256 MAX_NEST refusals and 170 MAX_EXPR_DEPTH refusals, both engines byte-identical on every one. Short chains (2..30 terms) also now appear inside ordinary programs via a p_chain knob, so the left-leaning shape is not confined to one flavour.

THE BUG IN MY OWN GENERATOR, found by disbelieving a stat. tree_limit sat at 0 while the generator looked like it was straddling MAX_EXPR_DEPTH. Cause: my chain mixed precedence rungs, and a mixed chain is NOT a left spine — %, * and / bind tighter than +, so 1 + 1 * 1 + 1 hangs small multiplicative subtrees off a SHORTER additive spine. A 12,000-operator mixed chain measured ~8,400 deep, sailed under the 10,000 cap, and evaluated to -189. Fixed: all operators in one chain come from one rung, additive for anything over 40 terms (* overflows within twenty terms and would end every long chain in the same place). Worth stating plainly because the coverage floors are the only thing standing between 'green' and 'green over nothing', and this is the second time a floor caught a generator that looked busy: the first was 1120 of 1600 programs dying in their first expression.

DELIVERABLE 2 — the experiment. The isolation rule held: six agents built two back ends without reading each other's source, and when one hit a question only the other group could answer it filed a spec gap instead of peeking. That is the precondition for the oracle meaning anything, and it survived pressure.

WHAT ACTUALLY PREVENTED DIVERGENCES was pinning things before the engines met, not the fuzzer finding them after. spec-adversary filed 14 gaps and pinned all of them, two of which would have guaranteed a divergence: '1000 frames' meant 999 user calls in one engine and 1000 in the other, and the frozen ast.rs referenced UnOp/BinOp which the spec never defined, so whoever landed first would silently have become the spec for six beads. §4's constructor discipline did the same job for message text — zero format! in production across all three engine files, and the two groups independently selected the SAME constructors for the builtins because neither engine can spell a message, only select one.

THE ORACLE'S LIMIT, learned the hard way: 35,200 programs found 0 divergences while the engines survived different recursion depths (tree returned 20001 where vm aborted). An abort yields no Output, so the comparison never happens. Differential testing is structurally blind to any failure that destroys the process. Fixed twice — the missing thread, then §6c making the asymmetry unreachable.
